n: The victorious Philistines carry the ark to Ashdod, one of their five chief cities near the Mediterranean coast, as a war trophy.

f.g: One of the five Philistine city-states, along with Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.

n: They place the ark in the temple of their god Dagon beside his statue, as if Israel's God were a captured god now serving theirs.

f.g: A major god of grain and fertility worshipped by the Philistines and others in the region.

n: The next morning Dagon's statue has fallen face down before the ark — as if bowing in worship to the Lord. The people set their god back up; a god who needs help standing is no god at all.
The following morning Dagon has fallen again, and this time his head and hands are broken off on the threshold. Head and hands symbolize thought and power — Dagon has neither before the Lord.

f.g: Literally “only Dagon was left” — just the trunk of the statue.

n: The narrator notes a local custom that came from this event: Dagon's priests and worshippers would not step on the temple threshold, even years later.
The Lord's “heavy hand” — His judgment — falls on Ashdod, striking the people with a painful plague of tumors.

f.g: tumors or swellings, possibly from a plague like bubonic plague (mice are mentioned in 6:4-5).

f.w: the hand of the LORD was heavy

n: The people of Ashdod realize Israel's God is behind their suffering and the humbling of Dagon. They want the ark gone.
The Philistine rulers meet and decide to move the ark to Gath, perhaps hoping the trouble was only local.

f.g: The rulers of the five cities; the word may be related to the Greek word “tyrant.”
Another Philistine city, later the hometown of Goliath.

n: In Gath the plague strikes everyone, young and old, with tumors and great panic. The Lord's power is not limited to one place.

f.g: everyone, from least to most important

n: They send the ark on to Ekron, but the Ekronites cry out in terror before it even settles in, convinced it has come to kill them.

f.g: The northernmost Philistine city, closest to Israelite territory.

n: The rulers meet again, and now the demand is clear: send the ark back to Israel. Death is spreading through the city.
Those who did not die suffer from tumors, and the city's cry of anguish rises to heaven. The captured ark has become the captors' greatest burden.

f.w: the cry of the city went up to heaven
